heroSub: 12 hand-picked Koh Mak stays across every level — 4-star beachfront resorts down to fan bungalows and easy-on-the-wallet hostels, spread across the main beaches Ao Suan Yai, Ao Kao and Ao Pra. From ฿700–6,500/night.
heroStats: 🏖️ 3 main beaches (Ao Suan Yai·Ao Kao·Ao Pra)
introH2: 🏝️ Why does choosing the right beach on Koh Mak matter?
introHtml: Koh Mak is a small, quiet island in the Trat sea — easy to ride a scooter all the way around — but each beach has its own feel. Ao Suan Yai on the north side has a long beach, clear water and sunset views, and several of the better resorts. Ao Kao on the southwest has fine white sand plus beachfront restaurants and bars within walking distance — the liveliest spot on the island. Ao Pra on the west is quieter and more private. Plenty of people book without checking which beach and then have to ride across the island for dinner every night. This guide rounds up 12 hand-picked Koh Mak places across every level — beach resorts down to fan bungalows and budget hostels — each with real guest reviews, a 3-site price compare and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Koh Mak has no public transport. Most places offer a pickup from the pier, and renting a scooter to ride around is the norm (small island, narrow concrete roads, easy riding). Getting there: take a boat from Laem Ngop pier in Trat — speedboat about 45–50 minutes, or ferry about 1.5 hours. Main beaches in this guide: Ao Suan Yai — long north-side beach, clear water, sunset views · Ao Kao — white sand, beachfront restaurants and bars, busiest stretch on the island · Ao Pra / Ao Nid — quiet and private · Low season (May–Oct) many places close to let the island recover, so check before you book.

entries.name: Seavana Koh Mak Beach Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Suan Yai beach · long beach, clear water, sunsets
entries.addr: Ao Suan Yai, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Top score in the 4-star group at 9.3 — Seavana is the best-balanced beachfront resort on Koh Mak, set on Ao Suan Yai with its long beach, clear water and full sunset views. Beachfront rooms step straight down to the sand from the terrace, and some have an in-room jacuzzi. Reviews praise the cleanliness, attentive staff and breakfast — a fit for couples and families who want a resort genuinely on the beach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, pick a Deluxe Beachfront and walk straight to the sand from your terrace — then sit on the beach at dusk for the sunset, the highlight of Ao Suan Yai.
pros: On Ao Suan Yai beach — long, clear water, sunset views
Highest score among the island's 4-star resorts
Beachfront rooms step to the sand; some have a jacuzzi
Reviews praise cleanliness and attentive staff
cons: Above the island average on price — best if you want true beachfront
Popular beachfront rooms sell out fast in high season

entries.name: Lazy Day The Resort
entries.addr: 49/9 Moo 1, Ao Kao beach, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Lazy Day is a beachfront bungalow resort on Ao Kao scoring a high 9.3 from 473 reviews. The draw is air-con bungalows facing the sunset side, a short step from the white-sand beach, on an Ao Kao stretch where beachfront restaurants and bars are within walking distance. Reviews praise the easygoing vibe, friendly staff and breakfast — a fit for couples and anyone who wants a beachfront stay without it feeling too polished.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Sunset bungalow facing the sea so you can catch the sunset from your terrace — and Ao Kao has beachfront spots you can walk to for dinner.
pros: Score 9.3 from 473 reviews — top of the bungalow group
Bungalows face the sunset side, steps from the sand
On Ao Kao, beachfront restaurants and bars within walking distance
Easygoing vibe, friendly staff, breakfast included
cons: Simple bungalows, not polished hotel rooms
Ao Kao beach gets busier than other beaches in high season

entries.name: Ao Kao White Sand Beach Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Kao beach · fine white sand
entries.addr: 60/1 Moo 1, Ao Kao beach, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Ao Kao White Sand is the most-reviewed resort on Koh Mak — over 1,280 reviews at a 9.1. It sits on Ao Kao's fine white sand with concrete villas that have private rooftops, a central pool, and beachfront rooms right on the sand. Reviews praise the beachfront location, value and atmosphere — and from just ฿1,500, it stands out on a popular beach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Garden View is the best value, but step up to a Beachfront Villa if you want to wake to the sea — and book early, as it's the island's most-booked resort.
pros: Most reviewed on the island — 1,280 reviews at 9.1
Ao Kao fine white sand, walking distance to beachfront spots
Villas with private rooftops + a central pool
From ฿1,500 — great value for a beachfront location
cons: Popular rooms sell out fast as the island's most-booked resort
Garden View doesn't face the sea — a short walk to the beach

entries.name: Mira Montra Resort Koh Mak
entries.addr: Ao Pra, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Mira Montra is a 4-star resort on Ao Pra on the quiet, private west coast, scoring 9.0. The standout is the Beachfront Villa right on Ao Pra — some with a bathtub and outdoor shower, some with a private rooftop. Reviews praise the calm, the villa feel and a location cut off from the bustle — a fit for couples who want privacy by the sea.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a quiet getaway, choose a Beachfront Villa to be right on Ao Pra; the hillside Deluxe rooms are cheaper but you'll walk down to the beach.
pros: On Ao Pra, the quiet and private west coast
Beachfront villas — some with bathtub and outdoor shower
Calm villa atmosphere, good for couples
Score 9.0 with reviews praising the privacy

Hillside Deluxe rooms aren't on the beach

entries.name: Plubpla Koh Mak Retreat
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Phai beach, south side · quiet
entries.addr: 50/5 Moo 2, Ao Phai beach, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Plubpla is a boutique sea-view villa resort with a solid 766 reviews at 8.6. The draw is garden villas facing the sea with outdoor showers, plus a handful of Beach Front Villas closest to the sand, set on the quieter south side of the island. Reviews praise the villa design, atmosphere and breakfast — a fit for couples who want a well-designed stay without a steep price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The few Beach Front Villas sell out fast, so book ahead; a Sea View Villa in the garden still gives you the sea and costs less.
pros: Boutique sea-view villas, well reviewed at 766
Outdoor showers, private atmosphere
On the quieter south side of the island
Breakfast included; reviews praise the design
cons: Only a few Beach Front Villas — they sell out fast

entries.name: Makathanee Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Kao beach · pool, on the sand
entries.addr: 63/14 Moo 1, Ao Kao beach, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Makathanee is the most-reviewed resort in this guide — over 1,749 reviews at 8.3. It sits right on Ao Kao with a pool and a wide range of rooms, from Pool/Sea View to Beach Bungalows and a Honeymoon Suite with a jacuzzi, from just ฿1,400 with breakfast. Reviews praise the value and the beachfront location in the heart of Ao Kao — a fit for families and groups who want a resort on the sand without paying a lot.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Groups get better value from the Family Suite, and the Panoramic Beach Bungalow opens onto a lawn down to the beach if you want to be closest to the sea.
pros: Most reviewed in this guide — 1,749 reviews
On Ao Kao beach with a pool
Wide range of rooms from ฿1,400, breakfast included
Reviews praise the value and beachfront location
cons: An older resort — some rooms are basic; pick a renovated one
Busy in high season as a popular Ao Kao choice

entries.name: Islanda Resort Hotel Koh Mak
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Suan Yai–Ao Kai headland · sea views
entries.addr: Moo 2, Ao Suan Yai–Ao Kai hillside, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Islanda is a 4-star boutique resort on the hillside between Ao Suan Yai and Ao Kai, scoring 8.7. The standout is the Ocean Terrace rooms, set above the pool with full sea views, plus a pool and family rooms. Reviews praise the sea views and the calm — and while the review count is still small as a lesser-known stay, it's a fit for anyone wanting a sea-view room at a sensible price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose a Deluxe Ocean Terrace or higher for a sea-facing balcony; Garden Terrace is cheaper but faces the garden.

entries.name: Koh Mak Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Suan Yai beach · on the sand
entries.addr: 1 Moo 2, Ao Suan Yai beach, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Koh Mak Resort is a beachfront bungalow resort on Ao Suan Yai that stands out for family rooms, scoring 8.3 from 250 reviews. The draw is Beachfront Bungalows you step to the sand from, plus 2-bedroom Family rooms for families or groups of friends, on Ao Suan Yai's long, clear-water beach. Reviews praise the beachfront location and sunset views — a fit for families travelling together who want a stay right on the sea.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Families get better value from a Family Beachfront room than booking several rooms, and Ao Suan Yai's long beach is great for an evening sunset stroll.

2-bedroom Family rooms, good for families

entries.name: Baan TaLay Hostel
entries.badge: 🏅 Top score, easy on the wallet
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Walking street, Ao Nid side · near the pier
entries.addr: 63 Walking Street, Koh Mak (Ao Nid side), Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Baan TaLay is the highest-scoring stay in this guide at 9.5. Despite being an easy-on-the-wallet hostel, it has private rooms with air-con and en-suite bathrooms — clean and compact, from just ฿1,100 — plus an on-site bar. It sits on the walking street on the Ao Nid side near the pier, so you can walk to food. Reviews praise the cleanliness, friendly owner and atmosphere — a fit for solo travellers or couples who want to keep costs down but still have a private room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick the Double with Terrace if you want a place to sit, and being near the walking street and pier means easy food on foot — no need to ride far.

entries.name: Monkey Island Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near Ao Kao beach · chilled vibe
entries.addr: Moo 1, near Ao Kao beach, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Monkey Island is the cheapest stay in this guide — fan bungalows from just ฿700 — with a big 760 reviews at 8.4. The draw is chilled wood-and-bamboo bungalows with hammocks on the terrace, a bar and a backpacker vibe near Ao Kao beach. Rooms range from fan with shared bathroom up to en-suite air-con and the group-friendly Gorilla Hut. Reviews praise the fun atmosphere and the price — a fit for budget travellers who want a real island feel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The ฿700 fan room is very cheap but uses a shared bathroom; step up to an Air-con Bungalow for more comfort, and groups can take the Gorilla Hut.

The draw is the Rim View rooms with big windows and wide sea-facing balconies, plus Sea View Villas for more privacy and Family Villas for larger groups. Reviews praise the sea views from the rooms — a fit for travellers who value the view more than being directly on the sand.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Standard room faces the garden; step up to a Rim View for the big windows and wide balcony — worth it for the view.

entries.name: The Cinnamon Art Resort and Spa
entries.addr: 26/9-10 Moo 2, Ao Nid area, Koh Mak, Koh Kood District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: The Cinnamon Art sells large wooden bungalows and the quiet of the Ao Nid area, scoring 7.9 from 120 reviews. The draw is the Thai Boutique Bungalow — a wooden bungalow around 85 sqm with a dressing area and indoor-outdoor bathroom — plus Beachfront Bungalows near a private beach and an on-site spa. Reviews praise the spacious bungalows and privacy, though some flag inconsistent upkeep — a fit for anyone who likes large wooden bungalows in a quiet corner.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick the Thai Boutique Bungalow for a large wooden bungalow with an outdoor bathroom, and check recent reviews on upkeep before booking in peak season.

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Koh Mak stays

faq.q: ❓ Which beach is best to stay on Koh Mak?
faq.a: It depends on your style. Ao Suan Yai has a long beach, clear water and sunset views with several good resorts (Seavana, Koh Mak Resort, Islanda). Ao Kao has fine white sand plus beachfront restaurants and bars within walking distance — the liveliest spot (Lazy Day, Ao Kao White Sand, Makathanee). Ao Pra / Ao Nid is quiet and private (Mira Montra, Cinnamon Art). On the island, renting a scooter makes getting between beaches easy.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Koh Mak stays cost?
faq.a: Quite a range: fan bungalows and hostels start around ฿700–1,400 per night; mid-range resorts and beachfront bungalows around ฿1,500–2,800; 4-star resorts and Beachfront Villas around ฿3,400–6,500. Rates swing a lot by season — high season and long weekends run higher than usual and rooms sell out fast.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Mak — which pier?
faq.a: Take a boat from Laem Ngop pier in Trat province — a speedboat takes about 45–50 minutes, or a ferry about 1.5 hours. Most places offer a pickup from the pier on the island; just mention it when booking. There's no public transport on the island, so renting a scooter to ride around is the norm — the concrete roads are narrow but easy since the island is small.

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time to visit, and does low season close?
faq.a: The best time is high season, November–April, with clear water and open skies. Low season, May–October is the rainy season with rougher seas, and many places close to let the island recover. If you go in low season, check with your accommodation that it's open and that boats are still running normally.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest to book a Koh Mak stay?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so open all three to compare before booking — every review page in this guide has price-compare links. Koh Mak stays sell out fast in high season, so booking ahead usually gets a better rate.

faq.q: ❓ Who is Koh Mak right for — is it too quiet?
faq.a: Koh Mak is a small island focused on quiet and nature, with no lively nightlife like the bigger islands. It suits couples, families and anyone wanting a real rest — riding a scooter around, snorkelling over coral, cycling. If you want parties and lots of venues, Koh Chang or another island may suit better; but for a calm sea, Koh Mak fits.
